title: Purpose, N-Year Vision, Next Milestone: a practical replacement for mission and vision statements
summary: Jason Cohen argues "mission" and "vision" are fuzzy terms and replaces them with three concrete tools: a Purpose bigger than the company, an N-year Vision (what you build, for whom, the insight), and a measurable Next Milestone. He also separates purpose-driven from purpose-derived companies, citing Smart Bear and WP Engine.

principles.text: Define Purpose as a transformation bigger than your company, about others, never fully achieved, and not a goal in your operating plan.
principles.quote: The transformation in the world that is bigger than ourselves, that we hope everyone involved is excited to help bring about.

principles.text: Welcome others who adopt your Purpose: they are allies, not competitors.
principles.quote: If others adopt the same purpose, we are happy. That isn't competition, that's an ally.

principles.text: Write the N-year Vision as what you built, for whom, and the special insight. Set N by company age divided by three, rounded up.
principles.quote: Rule of thumb: Divide the age of the company by 3, and round up.

principles.text: Keep the Vision to one or two sentences and bold but plausible; detail belongs in the strategy document.
principles.quote: The Vision should be clear, concise, declarative, and describe a specific future. Be bold, but plausible.

principles.text: Pick the Next Milestone by working backwards from the Vision, and make it specific with an objectively observable finish line.
principles.quote: The most important thing to achieve next, and how we'll know when we've arrived.

principles.text: You don't need to start purpose-driven. You can be purpose-derived: find the positive difference you make, state it, and build it into strategy and positioning.
principles.quote: What does create a Purpose, is figuring out the positive difference you can make in the world, then writing that succinctly, then incorporating it into your strategy and positioning and goals
